sources.title: Artemis II Preliminary Science Report
sources.finding: The report says the crew-described textural change at Orientale is apparent in the LOLA-derived roughness map but not in the Diviner-derived rock-abundance map. It interprets this as sensitivity to hectometer-scale terrain properties rather than the distribution of 1-2 m rocks.

sources.title: Artemis II Preliminary Science Report
sources.finding: Using the crew's inability to resolve a 2.5 km-wide rille unaided at 16,700 km and ability to see it through a 400 mm optical viewfinder, the report bounds unaided lunar-feature resolvability at greater than 0.5 and less than 3 arcminutes, or about 1-6 km nadir at pericynthion.

sources.title: Artemis II Preliminary Science Report
sources.finding: The report characterizes trained humans as contextual observers with a wide field of view and multi-scale perception, while calibrated instruments provide systematic quantitative measurement.

sources.title: Artemis II Preliminary Science Report
sources.finding: The report states that no handheld or vehicle camera was calibrated, color and photometric analysis is qualitative, and future missions should use calibrated imaging or spectroscopy plus a stable color reference.

sources.title: Artemis II Lunar Science Data User Guide
sources.finding: The guide says scheduled activity tags are usually assigned from timestamps, while primary and secondary target tags were manually applied to only a subset and were not thoroughly verified post-mission; errors may remain.

sources.title: Human perception of subresolution fineness of dense textures based on image intensity statistics
sources.finding: Controlled psychophysical experiments found that observers could discriminate subresolution texture fineness using diagnostic image-level intensity statistics. This establishes mechanism plausibility only; it does not validate the Artemis II case.
